title: The paper cup that's actually paper
standfirst: Nearly every takeaway cup in Britain has a layer of plastic inside it. Ours doesn't, and as far as we can tell we're the only ones in the country making them that way.
body:
Pick up whatever you drank your coffee out of this morning. Have a look inside it.

It feels like paper. It isn't, quite. There's a film of polyethylene bonded to the inside wall, because paper on its own gives up roughly four seconds after you pour hot coffee into it. That plastic is doing a real job.

It's also why the cup can't go in with the newspapers. To recycle it you have to separate the plastic from the fibre first, and hardly anywhere in the UK is set up to do that. So most cups never get recycled at all.

## We took the plastic out

Ours are lined with a water based coating instead. Keeps the drink where the drink should be. No polyethylene.

- 12oz and 16oz
- Single wall
- Double wall, for when the drink is hot enough that you'd rather not be holding it directly

As far as we know we're the only manufacturer in the UK making them this way, which is an odd thing to be able to say in 2026. We'd rather not be alone in it, frankly. If somebody else is doing it, tell us and we'll happily be wrong.

[image: /assets/img/cups-floating.jpg | 12oz and 16oz, single and double wall, printed on the same press as everything else that leaves here.]

## The bit nobody puts in the brochure

Coating behaves like a diva. Too thin and the cup weeps. Too heavy and it won't form properly on the machine. Dry it wrong and you get a pallet of cups welded into one very expensive tube.

We got there. It took considerably longer than we had planned, which is usually how these things go.

## Ordering them

They run through the same seven colour press as our cartons, with a coater, so the artwork lands the way you drew it rather than the way the machine fancied printing it that morning.

No minimum order. No maximum either. Two weeks from artwork to delivery is normal, and it arrives on our own vans.

Ring 01733 308000, or send the artwork over and we'll tell you what it will cost.
